store.29:
I took a sailing trip off the coast of Maine with a friend before my sophomore year. We stayed near Bar Harbor and spent a week exploring the coastal towns of New England. It was breathtaking. We'd wake up early, feel the crisp salt air, and watch the sunrise over the water. We'd sail past islands dotted with pine trees and enjoy breakfast on the deck, discussing our sailing routes for the day. We had a local instructor who taught us about navigation using both modern technology and old-school methods with star charts. It was thrilling to disconnect from my coding mindset and focus on the wind, tide charts, and the synergy between the boat and nature. We also had the best lobster rolls at a small dockside shack – still the best I've ever had. 

I also traveled to Japan during my junior year. I spent time in Tokyo, exploring the tech hub and marveling at the futuristic arcades and electronics stores in Akihabara. I tried to learn some Japanese phrases, but still ended up relying on gestures to order ramen. The food was incredible, and I was fascinated by the intersection in Shibuya, where thousands of people crossed the street in an orderly fashion. After Tokyo, I headed to Kyoto, which offered a completely different atmosphere – calm and steeped in history. I visited shrines and temples, and even caught a glimpse of geishas walking down a side street in Gion. It was surreal. Writing in my journal, I described Kyoto as feeling like stepping back into an older era, where craftsmanship and tradition take center stage. The sense of stillness and reverence left a lasting impression on me.
store.30: I took a family vacation to Europe last summer. We flew into London and spent a few days exploring the city. We visited the Tower of London, the British Museum, and rode the London Eye. My sister is a history buff, so she was thrilled to see the old artifacts and crown jewels. We also caught a musical in the West End, which was The Phantom of the Opera. It was one of the highlights of the trip. After London, we took a train to Paris. It was my first time in France, and although I barely remembered any French from middle school, it was easy to get around. The city is so picturesque, and the pastries were worth the trip alone. My favorite spot was strolling along the Seine River near Notre-Dame with a croissant in hand. It felt so relaxed compared to the hustle of London. We spent a day at the Louvre, which was amazing, but even that didn't feel like enough time. You could spend a week there and still not see everything.
store.31: I'm excited to plan a big trip before I graduate. I've been eyeing some internships in Silicon Valley for next summer, so if that pans out, I might spend a couple of weeks exploring the West Coast. I've heard great things about Portland, Seattle, and Vancouver – everyone always praises the coffee, craft beer, and beautiful scenery. If I line things up just right, I could do a road trip through Washington and Oregon after my internship ends, maybe with a friend or two who'll also be interning in the Bay Area. It would be awesome to discover the coastal highways, the Redwood forests, and those hidden beaches I keep seeing in photos. That might be my last chance to have a big chunk of free time before the post-grad grind starts.
